params.title: 2. Parameters Panel & 3. Training (Web Worker)
params.learningRateHint: Controls the step size when updating weights. Too low learns slowly; too high may overshoot and fail to converge.
params.epochsHint: How many times the network studies the entire dataset. More epochs lower error, but watch out for overfitting!
params.activationHint: Defines how a neuron transforms its weighted sum into output. Non-linear activations (ReLU, sigmoid, tanh) solve complex problems like XOR.
params.weightInitHint: How weights start before training. Breaking initial symmetry helps hidden neurons learn distinct roles.
params.biasHint: Shifts the activation function left or right, allowing the neuron to fire even when inputs are zero.
params.statusRunning: Training in Web Worker (60 fps UI)...

glossaryItems.def: A unit that receives inputs, multiplies each by a weight (w), adds bias (b), and applies an activation function.
Weight sets the strength and sign (+ or −) of a connection; bias shifts the firing threshold of the neuron.
An intermediate layer that, paired with non-linear activations (ReLU, sigmoid, tanh), solves problems not separable by a single line, like XOR.
Loss measures network error. Underfitting happens when the model is too simple or under-trained; overfitting happens when it memorizes noise.
In supervised learning the network imitates labeled examples; in reinforcement learning it learns via rewards and penalties.

quizQuestions.q: 1. What does an artificial neuron compute before applying its activation function?
options: The weighted sum of inputs multiplied by weights plus the bias
A purely random action ignoring inputs

quizQuestions.q: 2. Why does the XOR gate (Level 4) require a hidden layer?
options: Because it is not linearly separable by a single neuron
Because it only has 1 input sensor
Because bias does not work on logic gates

quizQuestions.q: 3. What happens if the learning rate is set too high?
options: Weight updates take oversized steps and loss may oscillate without converging
The number of sensors doubles automatically

quizQuestions.q: 4. How do we recognize good learning on the Loss chart?
options: The loss curve decreases over epochs until dropping below the target
In Levels 1–4 the network imitates labeled examples; in Level 5 it maximizes rewards and avoids penalties
Level 5 has no sensors or actions
Supervised learning does not use weights
